title: HubSpot static auth access token in an Authorization Bearer header
summary: A synthetic static auth access token after the Bearer scheme of an Authorization header, in a raw request, a curl option and a JSON header map.
rationale: HubSpot documents the static auth access token as the single-account credential of an app configured with auth type static and private distribution, found in the app settings and sent as a Bearer token (claims static-auth-token-exists, static-auth-selected-by-app-configuration). The Bearer header is shared with OAuth access tokens and legacy private app tokens, so the header does not identify the kind (claim bearer-carrier-shared-by-oauth-static-and-private-app-tokens) and no subtype is inferred. HubSpot's only example is a masked placeholder and the page states no prefix, alphabet, length or grouping (claim static-auth-placeholder-is-not-a-format-statement), so the fixture values are fixed markers. The relation to the legacy private app token and to Service Keys is unresolved (claim pages-do-not-relate-static-auth-and-private-app-tokens). The extent is the value after the scheme only. Contract claims cited: static-auth-access-token/static-auth-token-exists, static-auth-access-token/bearer-carrier-shared-by-oauth-static-and-private-app-tokens, static-auth-access-token/static-auth-placeholder-is-not-a-format-statement.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#243). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after the Bearer scheme of a static auth request is treated as a credential. HubSpot documents the credential and the Bearer carrier (carrier existence only); the value admission, the extent and the choice not to attribute a subtype are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: If you want to limit distribution of your app to a single authorized account, you'll use a static auth access token. This token can be found in your app settings.
This access token is provided using the Bearer HTTP authorization header.
An example request is provided below using a placeholder static auth access token.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy.
